headline: League Enters Week 3 Still Scoreless as Everyone Pretends the Waiver Wire Matters
meme_brief: Twelve grown men have been in a fantasy league for three straight weeks and literally nothing has happened — every game is 0.0 to 0.0, yet four different guys got into a bidding war over the same replacement-level running back like it was the last lifeboat off the Titanic.
recap: There is nothing to recap. For the third consecutive week, every matchup in Friends For Life finished 0.0 to 0.0 — Chuba Bucky Doo vs. mikelanta, Joe Mama Angie Daddy vs. Dak's Stack, Broke Dak Mountain vs. demon44, Waffle House vs. Geoff Collins Suvivor, Silverbacks vs. Pukachu Chews You, and Meredith's Fan Club vs. Screaming Eagles all ended in the exact same dead heat that's now defined the entire season. There is no closest game, because they are all equally close. There is no blowout, because nobody has scored a point. There is no top performer, because the box scores are a wall of zeroes from quarterback to kicker to defense. The worst bench decision of the week belongs to nobody and everybody, since bench and starting lineup have produced identical output across the board.
transaction_desk:
The actual football news this week happened on the waiver wire, where four separate teams — Joe Mama Angie Daddy, Meredith's Fan Club, mikelanta, and Pukachu Chews You — burned real waiver priority on the same running back, Mike Washington, in the same cycle. Three of those four now sit at the back of the priority order for a depth piece nobody can differentiate from the other three claims. Joe Mama Angie Daddy actually doubled up, using priority twice in the same week (Washington and Malik Davis) after already cutting Davis loose earlier in the process, which is either aggressive asset management or just not remembering who was already on the roster.

Elsewhere, the free-agent activity was low-cost and mostly harmless. Silverbacks churned through three depth moves (dropping and re-adding at receiver, plus a tight end swap for Hunter Henry) without spending a dime of priority, which is the correct way to hoard darts against a wire nobody's fighting over. Broke Dak Mountain added Najee Harris and Xavier Hutchinson for free, and Chuba Bucky Doo picked up a defense and a tight end the same way — uncontested, no priority burned, no real bet made either way. mikelanta was the week's most restless roster, cycling through a defense, two different wide receivers, and Isiah Pacheco before also joining the Mike Washington pile, though none of it cost anything since nobody else wanted the moves. With every add sitting at zero cumulative points through the young season, there's no heist or bust to report yet — just priority spent on a running back who, statistically speaking, has done as much as everyone else in this league so far. Nothing.

power_rankings.blurb: Unbeaten and scoreless, which is either a perfect record or a rounding error, and the commissioner's team is enjoying the ambiguity.

Sat out the transaction wire entirely and lost nothing for it, which says something about the state of the league.
Three moves, zero priority spent, mild chaos at receiver and tight end — patient roster building for a season that hasn't started scoring.
One quiet, sensible add at receiver. Boring is a strategy.

Made zero moves and still finished exactly as well as everybody who made several.

Joined the Mike Washington gold rush without dropping anyone, which at least kept the damage contained to priority.

No transactions, no points, no news — the quietest team in a league that has nothing but quiet.

standings_narrative: With six of twelve teams destined to make the postseason, the math is currently as simple as it will ever be: every team is 0-0 with 0 points for and against, meaning literally any team could claim to be in first place and be correct. There is no bubble yet because there is no separation — the moment one team scores an actual point, the entire complexion of these standings changes. Chuba Bucky Doo's technical unbeaten record is worth exactly as much as everyone else's technical unbeaten record, which is to say nothing, but expect that to be mentioned at the bar regardless.
look_ahead: Next week offers the same six matchups the league has already seen twice, presumably still waiting for football to actually be played and scored. Whichever team finally puts real points on the board will have a real claim to the league's first legitimate bragging rights of the season. Until then, keep an eye on the Mike Washington timeshare — four rosters now have a claim to him, and someone is going to have to actually start him for this whole exercise to mean anything.

running_jokes: The Great Zero enters its third straight week — no team in the league has scored a single point yet, across every single matchup, every single week.
